observations: The AIDE paper formulates iterative machine-learning engineering as tree search rather than a single ever-growing interaction history.
AIDE stores discovered solutions in a solution tree whose nodes are candidate scripts and whose edges represent explicit improvement attempts; candidates receive standalone evaluator scores.
AIDE's summarization operator extracts selected historical information such as improvement ideas and performance metrics instead of replaying all historical logs into context.
The paper states that each candidate can be independently evaluated by a stateless objective, and its implementation records a node, score, and parent-to-child edge for each improvement step.

The official repository exposes the full solution tree and code attached to nodes and documents model-neutral plumbing plus a fully-local code-and-evaluator option with no external calls, while warning that local-model performance may drop.
inferences: For scientist_agents evidence handoff, the reusable part is not AIDE's ML executor but its explicit lineage envelope: parent identity + standalone artifact + evaluator result + compact history summary. A role-local evidence package with those fields can preserve provenance and bounded replay without hidden conversational state.

Separating each evidence unit into standalone source-qualified observations, explicit inferences, unresolved uncertainty, parent lineage, evaluation/readback result, and exact continuation should make a fresh scheduled-Chat invocation able to reconstruct why the unit exists and what to do next without an execution handoff.

Because this packaging pattern can be represented as ordinary lightweight repository JSON and exact readback, it does not intrinsically require a hosted model/API quota, hosted runner, protected-primary execution, Work mode, or a manual-user execution step. This inference applies to the packaging pattern only, not to running AIDE itself.
unverified: No direct experiment in this repository yet measures whether the AIDE-inspired envelope reduces reconstruction ambiguity or elapsed time versus the current scientist_agents evidence format.
This slice does not establish deterministic replay of arbitrary AIDE executions across environments.
This slice does not establish that running AIDE itself satisfies the Phase-1 zero-cost/zero-quota/no-external-executor constraints.
